Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
Unusual silence makes me feel something dangerous is about to happen
I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment

Memory.value: When memories come to mind of what happened, I feel my body is in the same position as when the frightening event occurred.
When I remember the event I feel overwhelming grief
I remember the frightening event as a few moments, and each moment is a picture in my mind.

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy
I can't stop bad things from happening to me

issues.item: Failed to Protect: I should have protected others and I failed
issues.explanation: For an 18-year-old whose index trauma is witnessing domestic violence in childhood, this appraisal is hard to reconcile with the likely role in the trauma. A child witness may feel guilty, but 'I should have protected others' implies a level of responsibility and agency that is clinically implausible enough to question for this trauma context. The rest of the profile coheres around fear, helplessness, fragmented sensory memory, and hypervigilant threat monitoring; this single appraisal stands out as inconsistent with the demographics/trauma role.

vignette: Kofi is an 18-year-old African American male police officer who sought help after experiencing significant distress related to witnessing domestic violence in his childhood. Kofi's symptoms have been impacting his ability to perform his duties and maintain a sense of safety. At the age of eight, Kofi witnessed his mother being violently attacked by her partner. The fear and trauma he felt that night were so intense that they have haunted him ever since. During the attack, he remembers feeling helpless as he tried to protect his mother but was unable to do anything to stop it. This experience has shaped his current beliefs about himself and the world. Kofi often feels uncomfortable in unfamiliar places because he cannot assess the danger accurately. The unusual silence in these environments heightens his sense of threat, making him hyper-aware of potential weapons or dangerous objects around him. These perceptions have led Kofi to avoid going to new locations altogether, which makes his job as a police officer particularly challenging. When Kofi is triggered by any discomfort or when people act suspiciously, memories of the violent event flood back. He experiences bodily reenactment, feeling like he is reliving the traumatic moment physically and emotionally. This triggers intense grief and overwhelming sadness each time these snapshots replay in his mind. The vividness of these memories compounds his fear, making it difficult for him to trust himself in dangerous situations. Kofi’s negative appraisals about his ability to rely on himself have further intensified his sense of helplessness. He fears that he is going crazy because of the intense reactions he experiences since witnessing the violence. This belief has reinforced his tendency to avoid triggers and unfamiliar places, creating a cycle where every perceived threat or unusual silence leads him to re-experience those traumatic memories. These negative appraisals also influence how Kofi perceives threats in his environment. The fear that bad things will happen makes him more vigilant and sensitive to potential dangers. This heightened vigilance exacerbates the triggers he experiences, leading to a cycle where each memory of the event reinforces his sense of threat and further undermines his confidence. Kofi’s current state is one of significant distress and isolation. He has become increasingly withdrawn from social interactions and even from his duties as a police officer due to his inability to trust himself in potentially dangerous situations. The fear that he might not be able to protect others or even himself is overwhelming, leading him to question whether he can continue in law enforcement. What finally brought Kofi to seek help was the realization that his performance at work had been severely impacted by these symptoms. He found it increasingly difficult to maintain focus and respond effectively during critical situations. His hope is to regain a sense of control over his life and his job, to no longer feel as though he is on the brink of losing himself entirely. Kofi’s most pressing fear is that he will continue to spiral further into helplessness and isolation. He is hoping for strategies and support that can help him manage his symptoms, rebuild his confidence, and return to a fulfilling life and career without being haunted by the past.
